points.description: States that the star (*) operator is the dereferencing (indirection) operator.

levels.says: Describes dereferencing/indirection behaviour (e.g. 'accesses the value at an address') without naming it as the dereference operator, or names it but gives no further idea.

points.description: States that it returns the object/variable/value that its operand (a pointer / memory address) points to; i.e. the thing stored at that address. Accept 'the value at the address held by the pointer'. Do not accept 'the address of' the operand or 'the pointer itself' (confusing with & operator).

levels.says: Says it returns the value at an address but vague about the operand being a pointer.

points.description: States that the result is an alias (synonym) for the pointed-to object, i.e. another name for it that can be read or assigned to (an lvalue).

rubric.notes: Full marks need: dereference operator, returns the object the pointer operand points to, and that it acts as an alias/another name (lvalue). Part marks for correct but vague descriptions such as 'gets the value at the address'. No marks if the student says it returns the address of a variable or multiplication only.
